title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance + ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also contains a small set of linked ADRs for high-impact architecture decisions. The guidance is intended for product, platform, runtime, and infra teams responsible for building and operating inference services.

Audience:
- Engineering teams (platform, runtime, infra, SDKs)
- Product and security stakeholders planning integrations
- SRE/ops teams responsible for SLAs and runbooks

Scope:
Covers the following standards and decisions: API contracts and compatibility rules, code style and review expectations, cloud and on-prem infra patterns, model-serving runtime constraints and compatibility, observability and telemetry requirements, performance SLOs and testing guidance, and selected ADRs with canonical rationale.

Principles (applies cross-cutting):
- Backwards/forwards compatibility: maintain stable contracts, prefer additive changes, require explicit compatibility testing for breaking changes.
- Production-first: prioritize reliability, measurable SLOs, and clear rollback plans over premature optimization.
- Developer ergonomics: APIs and SDKs should be easy to use and consistent across environments (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Cost-awareness: design decisions should include expected cost impact and options to tune cost vs. latency/quality.
- Observability by default: every service exposes standardized telemetry and traces.

1) API standards
- Canonical contract: HTTP/1.1+ and gRPC endpoints (where low-latency multiplexing is required). Public REST endpoints must use JSON:API-compatible structures; internal high-throughput paths may use compact JSON or protobufs.
- Versioning:
  1. Use semantic versioning at the API surface (v1, v2).
  2. Additive changes (new fields) are allowed without bumping major; breaking changes require an ADR and 90-day deprecation window for hosted customers.
  3. Path-based versioning: /v1/generate, /v2/generate.
- Request/Response shape (generation example):
  - Request: {"model": "redwood-medium-001", "input": "...", "max_tokens": 128, "temperature": 0.2, "stream": false}  
  - Response: {"id": "req_12345", "model": "redwood-medium-001", "usage": {"input_tokens": 34, "output_tokens": 56}, "output": [{"type": "text", "content": "..."}], "warnings": []}
- Error handling:
  - Use HTTP status codes: 4xx for client errors (include error_code string), 5xx for server errors (include request_id).
  - All errors must include: message, error_code, request_id, docs_url.
- Rate limiting and quotas:
  - Default token-based rate limiting per API key and per route. Quotas must be declared in responses via headers: X-Quota-Limit, X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Reset.
- API compatibility tests: every change to public endpoints must include automated compatibility tests that exercise old SDK behaviors.

2) Coding standards
- Languages in scope: Go (platform/runtime), Python (SDKs, infra helpers), TypeScript (console & SDK), Rust/C++ (hot-path runtime modules).
- Formatting and linting:
  - Go: gofmt + golangci-lint with configured rule set (see repo .golangci.yml).
  - Python: Black, isort, flake8 (configured to Redwood rules).
  - TypeScript: Prettier + ESLint (Redwood config).
- PR expectations:
  - Minimum two reviewers (one owner + one cross-team reviewer) for changes to core services.
  - PRs must include: summary, design rationale, performance impact (tokens/sec, latency), testing plan, rollout steps, and rollback plan.
- Testing:
  - Unit tests: >= 80% coverage for new modules touching inference paths.
  - Integration: every change to serving/runtime must run in the local perf harness and pass end-to-end smoke tests.
- Secrets and credentials:
  - No secrets in repo. Use Vault/KMS integrations. Credential rotation documented in infra runbooks.

3) Infrastructure standards
- Environments: prod, staging, canary, dev. All environments must be reachable via internal DNS and have controlled network ACLs.
- Provisioning:
  - Terraform is the canonical IaC. Keep modules in eng-infra/terraform-modules.
  - Change control: non-trivial infra changes require a change request ticket and a canary rollout in staging followed by a 48-hour monitoring window.
- Networking:
  - Default svc-to-svc comms use mTLS (Mutual TLS) with automatic certificate rotation.
  - Cross-region failover: region priority list agreed per product; graceful DNS TTL-based failover required.
- Storage and data residency:
  - Customer data at rest must be stored according to region-specific controls; follow security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention guidance.
- Capacity and autoscaling:
  - GPU fleet autoscaler sets target based on queue depth and latency SLOs. Warm pools are required for headroom under 5xx spikes.

4) Model-serving standards
- Model packaging:
  - Models must be packaged with metadata: architecture, tokenizer version, quantization profile, input/output contract, and deterministic seed behavior. Metadata is a JSON metadata file shipped with model.
- Compatibility matrix:
  - Runtime supports architectures listed in runtime-architecture doc. Unsupported models must go through onboarding (model-onboarding) with perf and safety evals.
- Quantization and precision:
  - Default production profile for non-sensitive workloads: int8 quantization with per-channel scales when validated.
  - Sensitive/regulatory workloads default to fp16 with optional int8 after QA. See quantization-profiles for profile definitions.
- KV cache and session handling:
  - Long-running chat sessions must use per-session KV caching; TTL default 48h. Cache eviction policies must be deterministic and documented.
- Model rollouts:
  - Canary rollout (5% traffic) -> monitor for 24 hours -> 25% -> 50% -> full. Automated rollback on >2point5x error rate or >10% latency regressions.

5) Observability standards
- Metrics (all services must export):
  - request_count{route,model,region,tier}
  - request_duration_ms{p50,p90,p99}
  - token_emitted_count{model,route}
  - error_count{5xx,4xx,5xx_type}
  - queue_depth{worker_pool}
- Tracing:
  - Use W3C tracecontext headers; traces must embed model and request metadata (model, model_version, route, request_id).
- Logs:
  - Structured JSON logs with stable schema: timestamp, level, service, region, request_id, user_id (hashed), message, extras.
- Alerts and dashboards:
  - Standard dashboards exist per service (latency, error rate, cost/token).
  - Alert thresholds (examples):
    - p99 latency > SLO * 1.5 for 10m -> P1 oncall page.
    - error rate increase > 2x baseline for 5m -> P1.
- Sampling and retention:
  - Traces: sample 100% for canary traffic, 1% default for production, 100% for error traces.
  - Metrics retention: 90 days at 1m resolution, 3 years aggregated to 1h.

6) Performance standards and testing
- Latency SLOs (service-level defaults):
  - Generation (interactive): p50 < 50ms, p90 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms per token for short prompts (<=128 tokens) on Dedicated tier.
  - Batch inference: tail latency p95 < 2s for typical batch sizes.
- Throughput and capacity planning:
  - Use the GPU fleet capacity model (eng-sre/capacity-planning) to size clusters; ensure 25% spare headroom for burst absorption.
- Continuous benchmarking:
  - All runtime releases must include benchmark artifacts: token/sec, latency percentiles, memory usage, and cost-per-1k-output-tokens. Store results in benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
- Performance regressions:
  - Any change that regresses p90 by >10% compared to release baseline requires an ADR-style exception and a monitored rollout.

7) Release and rollout process (high level)
- Preflight: integrate unit/integration tests, run perf harness, run compatibility suite.
- Canary: 5% traffic for 24 hours with full observability snapshot.
- Rollout gating: SLO checks (latency, error rate, resource usage), manual sign-off for infra/infra-impacting changes.
- Rollback: automated rollback triggers and documented playbook in runbooks.

8) ADRs (Decision records)
- ADR-2026-03: Default API contract and versioning\  - Date: 2026-03-01\  - Status: accepted\  - Context: Need consistent API contract for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments to reduce SDK fragmentation and runtime compatibility issues.\  - Decision: Adopt path-based versioning (/v1/) with semantic API compatibility rules: additive changes allowed, breaking changes require major version bump and 90-day deprecation window. Support both REST (JSON) and gRPC for internal high-throughput paths.\  - Consequences: SDKs require version pinning; compatibility tests added to CI; increased maintenance on supported versions.\  - Owners: API platform team (owner: Priya Kaur)
\
- ADR-2026-03-Quantize: Default production quantization strategy\  - Date: 2026-03-10\  - Status: accepted\  - Context: Improve throughput/cost while limiting quality regressions.\  - Decision: Default non-sensitive workloads to int8 per-channel quantization validated by model-specific QA; sensitive/regulatory workloads use fp16 by default.\  - Consequences: Requires per-model quantization profiles, additional QA cycles at onboarding, and runtime support for mixed-precision execution paths.\  - Owners: Serving runtime team (owner: Daniel Kim)

9) Governance and exceptions
- Standards review cadence: quarterly review by architecture board (eng leads + product + security).
- Exceptions: Ad hoc exception requests submitted to architecture board with: rationale, impact analysis, mitigation plan, and sunset date. Exceptions greater than 6 months require reapproval.

10) Onboarding checklist (for new services or major changes)
1. Draft design doc and link to this standard.
2. Run compatibility matrix and identify impacted SDKs.
3. Add metrics/tracing instrumentation as specified.
4. Add perf harness job and baseline artifact.
5. Schedule canary and set rollout playbook.
6. Add runbook entry and oncall escalation contacts.

Appendices
A. Standard metric tags and labels (example):
- service, env, region, model, model_version, tier, route

B. Example alert thresholds (tunable per service):
- p99 latency > 2s for 5m -> P1
- 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m -> P1
- queue_depth > 100 for 5m -> P2

C. Useful links:
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture
- applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
- eng-infra/terraform-and-iac
- security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention

If you propose a change to any of the above, open an ADR and follow the ADR template in decision-records. For immediate clarifications, contact the architecture board via #arch-board on Slack or email arch-board@redwood-inference.internal.
